residual_risks: INJECTION RESISTANCE IS NOT PROVEN AND IS NOT PROVABLE DRY-RUN. What this packet proves is that the <repo_content> delimiter and the untrusted-data preamble are UNIFORMLY APPLIED at every prompt-assembly path (choke point + sync dispatch + async R dispatch + strict-repair by reuse). Whether a given model actually honours the boundary against a determined injection is an empirical property of the model and requires live adversarial evals. A delimiter is a mitigation, not a guarantee.

The boundary is a delimiter, not a filter: untrusted content is still passed to the model verbatim (by design — the extractor must read it). A payload containing a literal '</repo_content>' string could attempt delimiter-escape/confusion. No escaping or neutralisation of the closing tag inside file bodies is performed. Not exploited or tested here; flagged as the natural follow-up hardening.

The 136 template convention lines are static documentation. If a future template is added without the '## Inputs' convention line, FA-3 still passes (it only requires >=1 template to carry a delimiter token), so template coverage can silently regress. The runtime wrap is unaffected by this and remains the real defense.

PAL chain (analyze/planner/codereview/precommit) NOT_RUN — this change has had no independent multi-model review. Given it touches a security-relevant shared choke point in a 22k-line module, a codereview pass before merge is advisable.
